Subject: Dedicated fleet sizing — quick kickoff and questionnaire request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency numbers looked promising. We are starting internal planning for a pilot that will run in Q4 and procurement asked me to gather a formal sizing questionnaire so they can align budget and timelines.

Can you share Redwood's pre-sales sizing template (traffic, concurrency, typical prompt/response length breakdowns, and any required performance SLOs you assume when sizing a dedicated fleet)? Also, any notes on SKU recommendations for burst vs steady-state would be helpful — our product team expects a steady 40 TPS with spiky peaks to 220 TPS for short bursts.

Attaching our initial SLO doc for context (internal). Let me know if you want to set a short call to walk through.

Appreciate it,
Tom Keller
Director of Platform Engineering
Astra Retail
Attachment: astra_slo_requirements.pdf (pdf, 412KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing — quick kickoff and questionnaire request

Tom —

Thanks — appreciate the context and the SLO doc. I’m attaching our updated pre-sales questionnaire (redwood_dedicated_questionnaire_v2.docx) which gathers the details our infra sizing engine uses. To be efficient, could you answer the bolded bits below and return the CSV with a few representative weekday/weekend samples if possible? That will let us produce an initial SKU mapping and cost/latency envelope.

Key items we need (short version):
- Traffic profile: average requests/sec, 95th/99th percentiles, and expected monthly peak-day RPS.
- Concurrency: number of concurrent user sessions hitting the model and average token-generation concurrency per session.
- Prompt/response lengths: median and 95th percentile prompt tokens and generated tokens per request.
- Model choices: are you planning to run a single large LLM for all intents or a two-tier setup (small models for classification/rerank + large for generation)?
- Quality SLOs: p95 latency target (ms) for interactive flows and batch/async targets if any.
- Data residency & networking: expected region and whether you will use VPC Private mode.

We can produce a conservative SKU recommendation or an aggressive one depending on whether cost or headroom matters more. Based on your note (steady 40 TPS, spikes to 220 TPS), my back-of-envelope would be a mix of reserved GPU capacity sized for ~120 TPS steady with burst pool for peaks, but I’d prefer to validate with the sample traffic.

If it helps, I can loop in Dev (SE) to sketch a preliminary mapping to specific GPU SKUs and estimated monthly cost. Want me to include him on the next mail?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0123
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_questionnaire_v2.docx (docx, 98KB)

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated fleet sizing 96 Astra Retail 

Folks, forwarding Astra's ask and the draft SLO. High level notes / proposed assumptions for a first pass SKU map: 

- Customer profile: steady 40 TPS, 95th around 90 TPS, short bursts to 220 TPS (10-15 minutes), estimated monthly active sessions ~120k.
- Primary use: conversational shopping assistant (multi-turn), median prompt ~150 tokens, median generated tokens ~120 tokens, 95th prompt 600 tokens, 95th gen tokens 400 tokens.
- Proposed model strategy: two-tier. Small encoder model for intent/classification + a mid-large ~20B gen model for full responses. This reduces token-generation load on the largest SKUs.
- Fleet SKU suggestion (preliminary): reserve N x A800s (or equivalent) for steady-state concurrency 120 TPS; keep a small burst pool of 6 A100-80GB equivalents for peaks and for cold-start fast fallbacks.
- Autoscaling policy: warm pool threshold at 75% token concurrency, scale-to-zero disabled for pilot.
- Network: prefer VPC Private with egress peering (customer asked for data residency).

Action items: Dev — can you run a quick simulation on these assumptions and return expected p95 token latency and estimated monthly GPU hours? Karthik 97 can you draft a short canary rollout plan and note any constraints for A800 vs A100 mixes we should flag to procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick reply and the questionnaire. Attached is a small sample of our traffic (astra_sample_traffic.csv) and an annotated version of our SLO doc with answers to your bolded items. A few clarifications inline:

- Steady-state 40 TPS is measured across our global edge (we expect ~65% of traffic to land in us-west initially).
- Concurrent sessions: we estimate 1.8 concurrent token-generation streams per active session at peak.
- Token distributions are attached in the CSV (columns: interval, reqs, median_prompt_toks, median_gen_toks, p95_prompt, p95_gen).
- For the pilot we can accept p95 latency of 600ms for interactive flows; lower is better but procurement budget is sensitive.
- We prefer reserved capacity for baseline SLA, with a 2-week burst pool for new campaign spikes.

We are happy to hop on a short call to review the recommended SKUs after you run your initial mapping.

Regards,
Helen R.
Program Manager, Platform Ops
Astra Retail
